about: The Ultimate Challenge's own rounds: never played on the Board or in Defuse. Cambridge formats only, written around the traps B2 First actually sets.

rounds.prompt: The streets are wet. It ___ during the night.
rounds.note: must have + past participle: you're sure, from the evidence.

rounds.prompt: She ___ the email — she replied to it ten minutes later.
rounds.note: She replied, so you're certain: must have read.

rounds.prompt: He ___ the answer; he's never studied chemistry.
rounds.note: can't have + past participle: you're sure it didn't happen.

rounds.prompt: You ___ me you were coming! I'd have made dinner.
rounds.note: should have + past participle: criticising what didn't happen.

rounds.prompt: I ___ so much food — half of it is still in the fridge.
rounds.note: needn't have bought: you did it, but it wasn't necessary.

rounds.prompt: We ___ a taxi, but we decided to walk.
rounds.note: could have + past participle: a possibility that wasn't chosen.

rounds.prompt: I'm not sure where my keys are. I ___ them at school.
rounds.note: might have + past participle: perhaps it happened.

rounds.prompt: Luckily, we ___ queue — we already had tickets.
rounds.note: didn't have to + verb: it wasn't necessary, so we didn't.

rounds.prompt: You ___ driven so fast. You could have had an accident.
rounds.note: shouldn't have + past participle: it was wrong to do it.

rounds.prompt: The window is broken, but it ___ the cat — it was locked in the kitchen.
rounds.note: The cat was locked in, so it's impossible: can't have been.

rounds.prompt: He looks really tired. He ___ up late last night.
rounds.note: Evidence now, conclusion about the past: must have stayed.

rounds.prompt: I ___ to the party, but I wasn't invited.
rounds.note: would have + past participle: what you'd have done in other circumstances.

rounds.prompt: She ___ the bus — it left before she got to the stop.
rounds.note: The bus left before she arrived, so: must have missed.

rounds.prompt: They ___ lost; they had a map and a phone.
rounds.note: A map and a phone make it impossible: can't have got lost.

rounds.prompt: I ___ harder for the test. I'm sure I failed.
rounds.note: should have + past participle for a regret.

rounds.prompt: Where's Tom? He ___ forgotten about the meeting, I suppose.
rounds.note: may have + past participle: a possible explanation.

rounds.prompt: You must ___ been very proud when you won the prize.
rounds.note: must have been: a confident guess about a past feeling.

rounds.prompt: I didn't ___ to wear a uniform at my old school.
rounds.note: didn't have to / didn't need to: it wasn't necessary.

rounds.prompt: We ___ have hurried; the train was delayed anyway.
rounds.note: needn't have hurried: we did, but it turned out unnecessary.

rounds.prompt: You ___ to have told me earlier — now it's too late.
rounds.note: ought to have + past participle = should have.

rounds.prompt: I'm not sure, but he ___ have taken the earlier train.
rounds.note: may / might / could have: a possibility.

rounds.prompt: We had ___ leave early because my brother felt ill.
rounds.note: had to: past necessity.

rounds.prompt: It ___ have been Ana you saw — she's in Spain this week.
rounds.note: can't have been: you're sure it's impossible.

rounds.prompt: If you had asked me, I ___ have lent you my bike.
rounds.note: would / could have + past participle in an unreal past.

rounds.prompt: The door was open. Someone must have forgotten ___ lock it.
rounds.note: forget to + verb: not doing something you should.

rounds.prompt: He ___ not have heard you; he had his headphones on.
rounds.note: may not / might not have heard: perhaps he didn't. Couldn't have heard: he certainly didn't.

rounds.prompt: You needn't ___ brought a present, but thank you!
rounds.note: needn't have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: She was supposed ___ call me, but she forgot.
rounds.note: be supposed to: what was expected but didn't happen.

rounds.prompt: They must have been waiting ___ ages before the doors opened.
rounds.note: must have been waiting for ages: a continuous deduction.

rounds.prompt: I wish I ___ listened to your advice.
rounds.note: wish + past perfect for a past regret.

rounds.prompt: I'm sure Ana forgot about the meeting.
rounds.note: I'm sure … = must have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: It's impossible that he saw us; it was too dark.
rounds.stem: He ___ us; it was too dark.
rounds.note: impossible = can't have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: It was a mistake to tell her the secret.
rounds.note: a mistake = shouldn't have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Perhaps they took the wrong road.
rounds.note: perhaps = might have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: It wasn't necessary for you to wash the car, but thanks.
rounds.note: You did it, but it wasn't necessary: needn't have washed.

rounds.prompt: It was possible for us to win, but we were unlucky.
rounds.note: a possibility that didn't happen: could have won.

rounds.prompt: I regret not going to the concert with you.
rounds.stem: I ___ to the concert with you.
rounds.note: regret not doing = should have done.

rounds.prompt: Why didn't you tell me about the problem?
rounds.note: ought to have + past participle = should have.

rounds.prompt: I'm sure it wasn't Paul who broke it; he wasn't even here.
rounds.stem: It ___ Paul who broke it; he wasn't even here.
rounds.note: sure it wasn't = can't have been.

rounds.prompt: It wasn't necessary for us to buy tickets in advance, so we didn't.
rounds.note: Not necessary, and we didn't: didn't have to.

rounds.prompt: Maybe she didn't hear the doorbell.
rounds.note: maybe … didn't = may not have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: It was wrong of you to leave without saying goodbye.
rounds.note: wrong of you = shouldn't have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: I'm sure he was very tired after the race.
rounds.stem: He ___ very tired after the race.
rounds.note: I'm sure he was = he must have been.

rounds.prompt: I didn't go to the party because nobody invited me.
rounds.stem: I ___ to the party if somebody had invited me.
rounds.note: Third conditional result: would have gone.

rounds.prompt: You were supposed to phone me last night.
rounds.note: be meant to = be supposed to.

rounds.prompt: There's a chance that I left my wallet on the bus.
rounds.stem: I ___ my wallet on the bus.
rounds.note: there's a chance = could have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: You ___ told me about the test! I didn't study at all.
rounds.note: Could have: annoyed criticism of the past.

rounds.prompt: She ___ forgotten our meeting — she's never late.
rounds.note: Sure it happened: must have.

rounds.prompt: He ___ been at the party; he was in Paris that night.
rounds.note: Sure it didn't happen: can't have.

rounds.prompt: We ___ taken a taxi — the station was only five minutes away.
rounds.note: Done, but unnecessary.

rounds.prompt: I'm not sure where Tom is. He ___ gone home early.
rounds.note: Perhaps: might have.

rounds.prompt: You ___ so rude to your grandmother.
rounds.note: Criticism: shouldn't have.

rounds.prompt: The streets are flooded. There ___ a storm last night.
rounds.note: Evidence → must have been.

rounds.prompt: I ___ better if I'd had more time.
rounds.note: Possible but unreal: could have.

rounds.prompt: They ___ won the match — they were losing 3–0 with a minute to go.
rounds.note: Impossible: can't have.

rounds.prompt: We ___ to bring our passports, so we left them at home.
rounds.note: Not necessary, so not done: didn't have to.

rounds.prompt: The window is broken. Someone ___ it with a ball.
rounds.note: Evidence → must have.

rounds.prompt: You ___ the oven on! The cake is burnt.
rounds.note: A past mistake: shouldn't have.

rounds.prompt: She ___ have seen us — she waved.
rounds.note: She waved → she must have seen us.

rounds.prompt: I ___ have locked the door — I can't remember.
rounds.note: Perhaps not: may not have.

rounds.prompt: He ___ apologised — that would have solved everything.
rounds.note: A possibility that didn't happen.

rounds.prompt: You ___ worried about me — I was fine.
rounds.note: The worry wasn't necessary.

rounds.prompt: It ___ been Ana you saw; she's abroad.
rounds.note: Impossible: couldn't / can't have.

rounds.prompt: We ___ the wrong turning — this isn't the right road.
rounds.note: Evidence → must have.

rounds.prompt: You should have ___ me the truth.
rounds.note: Should have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: He can't ___ seen me; I was hiding.
rounds.note: Can't have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: They might have ___ lost in the forest.
rounds.note: Might have got lost.

rounds.prompt: You ___ not have brought flowers, but thank you.
rounds.note: Need not have: unnecessary.

rounds.prompt: I could ___ helped you if you'd asked.
rounds.note: Could have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: There ___ have been an accident — the road is closed.
rounds.note: A deduction about the past.

rounds.prompt: I'm sure Ana left early.
rounds.note: Sure + past → must have.

rounds.prompt: It's possible that he didn't get my message.
rounds.note: Perhaps not → might not have.

rounds.prompt: It was a mistake to tell him.
rounds.note: A past mistake → shouldn't have.

rounds.prompt: It's impossible that they finished already.
rounds.note: Impossible → can't have.

rounds.prompt: You washed the car, but it wasn't necessary.
rounds.note: Done but unnecessary → needn't have.

rounds.prompt: Why didn't you ask me for help?
rounds.note: Criticism → could have.
